_comment: A small curated reference set of well-known on-chain risk patterns. This is static reference material, not a live feed — the Watcher agent is the one that decides whether current evidence matches any of these, and explains the match in its own words. Nothing here maps directly to a rating.

patterns.name: Coordinated liquidity withdrawal
patterns.description: A large share of pool liquidity (commonly 50-100%) is removed in a single transaction or within a short window, well after the token's early/volatile period has passed. Distinct from normal early-stage liquidity thinness because it represents a sudden reversal in an asset that had established trading history.
typicalSignals: token age > 30 days at time of drop
LP tokens concentrated in one or few wallets before the drop

patterns.name: Hidden or abused mint function
patterns.description: Contract retains an unrestricted or owner-only mint function that gets called post-launch to inflate supply, diluting holders or enabling a dump.
typicalSignals: sudden large supply increase not disclosed in advance
mint event from an EOA shortly before a price/liquidity drop
historicalExamples: Various unaudited fork tokens, recurring pattern since 2020

patterns.name: Fake or partial ownership renounce
patterns.description: Project claims ownership was renounced (marketed as a safety signal) but retains a privileged role via a proxy admin, secondary owner-like address, or unrenounced minter/pauser role.
typicalSignals: owner() returns zero address but a separate privileged role still exists
upgradeable proxy pattern with an active proxy admin

patterns.name: Oracle / price manipulation via low liquidity
patterns.description: An attacker manipulates a thin, single-source price feed (often a low-liquidity DEX pool used as an oracle) to distort collateral or reward calculations, typically via flash loan.
typicalSignals: asset price used as an oracle input has thin liquidity
large, brief price spike reverting shortly after

patterns.name: Stablecoin/RWA reserve shortfall
patterns.description: A stablecoin or RWA-backed token's attested reserves fall below its circulating supply, or Proof-of-Reserve data goes stale/unavailable during a period of stress.
typicalSignals: Proof of Reserve value < circulating supply
PoR feed not updated for an unusually long time
redemption delays or withdrawal limits announced

patterns.name: Team activity cliff
patterns.description: Public team/dev activity (commits, governance posts, social presence) drops sharply and stays silent, often preceding abandonment or an exit.
typicalSignals: no public commits/posts for an extended period after a previously active cadence
team wallets move funds shortly before or during the silence
